To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the power dissipation in a 1-bit full adder cell is dominated by the power dissipation of the XOR gate, the power dissipation is reduced when the XOR gate is implemented using a transmission gate, the power consumption of the carry logic is reduced when a transmission gate is implemented in series with the carry logic, and the power consumption of an adder cell is reduced when the adder is implemented using a carry-select adder.
the 1-bit full adder is a critical building block in the design of low-power high-speed circuits.

1) the full-adder cells that are based on the XOR gate are the most power efficient, 2) the full-adders that are based on a 1-bit adder are the fastest, 3) the full-adds that are based on an AND gate are the most area efficient, and 4) the full-add cells based on a NOR gate have the highest driving capability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a full-adder cell for use in a 64-bit adder/subtractor.
the design of low-power 0.18-mum CMOS full-adder cell and the development of a library of such cells.
developing low-power, high-speed, high driving capability and small-area full adder cells and circuits that are suitable for VLSI and ultra-large VLSI applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the 1-bit full adder cells are the most important cells in digital circuits, and they are very important in low-power circuits, especially in low-power digital signal processing (DSP) circuits.
the proposed full-adder cell design is a very good choice for low-power and low-speed applications.
, the proposed 1-bit full adder cells have a very low power consumption and are suitable for low-power applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a library of 1-bit CMos full-adder cells that exhibit a wide range of power-speed-area figures.
the full-adder design is a very important circuit block in the digital systems and the full-adder circuit design has a significant effect on the overall system performance.
the proposed full-adder cells have the lowest power consumption, area, and delay figures among all the full-adder cells reported in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the adder cell is not only a function of the design of the cell itself, but also a function of the structure that the cell is embedded in.
the power dissipation of a full-adder cell can be reduced significantly (by a factor of 3) without any noticeable degradation in the speed and the driving capability.
there is no single full-adder cell design that is best for all applications.
